facts.text: Strawberry earned its name from the wild strawberries that flourished in the area when settlers first arrived.
Gold discovered in the hills around 1875 sparked a wave of settlers and turned Strawberry into a mining hub.
The Strawberry Schoolhouse, built in the late nineteenth century, now houses a local history museum and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The town sits in the valley of Strawberry Creek, part of the Verde River watershed, giving it a distinctive natural setting.
In June 1931, a large whiskey still in Sandrock Canyon north of Strawberry was destroyed by the Bureau of Prohibition, a notable event in the town’s prohibition history.
Strawberry’s historic charm is highlighted by the Pine‑Strawberry Museum, which showcases the prehistoric and historic heritage of both Pine and Strawberry.
